principle: The design reference and its design system take precedence over stylistic preference. An element is slop only when it was added without source evidence, design-system backing or a functional requirement; unsupported additions are removed or replaced, never defended with taste.

indicators.name: Tags and pills
indicators.summary: Small rounded labels that fragment content into decorative chips instead of conveying state or filtering.
signals: rounded-full tag rows
status pills with invented states
pill-shaped badges beside every heading
chips used as decoration rather than filtering or state
indicators.notes: Pill-shaped buttons, tags and status chips are legitimate when the reference shows them or the design system defines them. Flag pill soup, not a single reference-backed pill.

indicators.name: Excessive italics
indicators.summary: Italic type used as a default emphasis or display style rather than a deliberate editorial choice.
signals: italicised body paragraphs
italic display headings
italics used for emphasis on every second line
fake handwritten italic quotes
indicators.notes: Quotations, book titles and source-backed editorial styling may use italics. Replace decorative italics with the design system's emphasis weight or colour.

indicators.name: Instrument Serif or unjustified fashionable typography choices
indicators.summary: Trend-led display typefaces, especially Instrument Serif, swapped in without reference or token support.
signals: font-family: 'Instrument Serif'
fashionable display serif swapped in without a reference
mixed serif and sans pairing with no design-system token
new webfont added to match a current portfolio trend
indicators.notes: A typeface is justified by the reference, a brand token or an explicit user requirement. Fashion alone is not evidence.

indicators.name: Negative kerning
indicators.summary: Tight or negative letter-spacing applied by default to make headings look designed.
signals: letter-spacing with negative values on headings
tracking-tighter applied globally
overlapping glyphs at display sizes
negative em tracking without a design token
indicators.notes: Large display type may legitimately use a measured negative tracking value. Copy the reference measurement instead of guessing.

indicators.name: Over-the-top detailed UI
indicators.summary: Dense invented chrome, nested panels and decorative controls that exceed the information the interface carries.
signals: nested cards three levels deep
invented toolbars and control clusters
decorative panel chrome around simple content
multi-layer glass effects
indicators.notes: Complexity must map to real content or real interaction. Remove decorative controls that do nothing.

indicators.name: Excessive dividers
indicators.summary: Rules and separators between almost every element, creating rhythm where spacing should do the work.
signals: horizontal rules between every list item
section dividers on every block
border-top and border-bottom pairs used as rhythm
dividers added to empty decorative space
indicators.notes: A divider is justified by grouping semantics or the reference. Prefer spacing when the only goal is separation.

indicators.name: Unnecessary colour shades and opacity variations
indicators.summary: Extra near-identical greys and arbitrary opacity steps that bypass the colour tokens.
signals: five near-identical grey values
opacity variants standing in for tokens
text-white/60 next to text-white/70 in the same group
extra colour shades introduced for one element
indicators.notes: Use the token scale. Opacity may encode a real state, such as disabled or muted metadata, when the reference or design system defines it.

indicators.name: Unnecessary bordered containers
indicators.summary: Outlines wrapped around plain content so the page reads as boxes inside boxes.
signals: border on every card and nested card
outlined boxes around plain text
double borders between adjacent regions
borders added only to make a layout feel finished
indicators.notes: A border is justified by a component definition, a state boundary or the reference. One container level is usually enough.

indicators.name: Overly detailed diagrams
indicators.summary: Invented node graphs and flowcharts that decorate the page without representing real data or architecture.
signals: invented architecture diagrams
decorative node graphs with no data source
over-labelled flowcharts that restate the copy
diagram connectors added for visual texture
indicators.notes: Diagrams may be required to explain a real system or sequence. Every node must correspond to something real.

indicators.name: Verbose and redundant text
indicators.summary: Copy that restates the heading, repeats claims or explains what the interface already shows.
signals: three sentences saying the same thing
feature lists that repeat the heading
long explanatory paragraphs under every label
filler introductions before the actual content
indicators.notes: Legal, safety and compliance text can be irreducible. That is a functional requirement with a reference, not permission for marketing padding.

indicators.name: Unnecessary code breadcrumbs
indicators.summary: File paths, component trails or step crumbs placed above snippets to signal technical credibility.
signals: src/components/... above a snippet
Step 1 > Step 2 > Step 3 breadcrumbs on static copy
file-path captions added for atmosphere
component-name labels above every block
indicators.notes: Breadcrumbs are appropriate for real navigation or a real code example that benefits from its path. Decorative paths are not.

indicators.name: Arbitrary section numbering
indicators.summary: 01 / 02 / 03 labels attached to sections that have no required reading order.
signals: 01 / 02 / 03 labels on unordered sections
numbering generated from list index
section counters with no reading sequence
large numerals used as decoration
indicators.notes: Ordered steps, legal clauses and ranked lists have real sequences. Marketing sections usually do not.

indicators.name: Unrequested eyebrows
indicators.summary: Small kicker labels above headings that repeat the heading or add a category nobody asked for.
signals: small uppercase kicker above every heading
category label restating the heading
eyebrow text with no informational role
kicker added to introduce a section that already has a title
indicators.notes: Eyebrows can carry real hierarchy when the reference or design system uses them. Do not add one to every section by default.

indicators.name: Dithering
indicators.summary: Dither or noise textures applied to flat surfaces to make them feel tactile.
signals: noise or dither texture overlays
background-image dither patterns
halftone overlays on flat surfaces
grain layers added over every section
indicators.notes: A reference may use a deliberate print or dither aesthetic. Reproduce that texture only when it is evidenced.

indicators.name: ASCII images
indicators.summary: Text-art illustrations and box-drawing graphics used in place of real imagery.
signals: ASCII art illustrations
box-drawing characters used as imagery
text-art logos
terminal-style banners standing in for a hero image
indicators.notes: ASCII belongs to terminal products and source-backed developer aesthetics. It is not a substitute for missing photography.

indicators.name: Unnecessary squircles
indicators.summary: Superellipse masks applied to icons, avatars and images as a stylistic default.
signals: superellipse masks on icons and avatars
squircle clip-path applied globally
rounded-square image masks with exaggerated corner smoothing
iOS-style icon masks in a non-iOS interface
indicators.notes: Squircles belong to platforms and systems that specify them. Otherwise use the component library's radius token.

indicators.name: Excessive monospace typography
indicators.summary: Monospace used as a personality layer for headings, labels and body copy that is not code.
signals: font-family: monospace for body copy
mono labels on non-technical content
mono used to signal technical style
mono applied to navigation and buttons
indicators.notes: Code, tokens, measurements and tabular data may need monospace. A developer-tool brand may specify it. Decorative mono does not.

indicators.name: Unnecessary ALL-CAPS subtitles
indicators.summary: Uppercase subtitles and labels added for emphasis when sentence case already carries the hierarchy.
signals: uppercase subtitle under every heading
ALL-CAPS section labels used as decoration
letter-spaced uppercase strings
uppercase micro-labels with no design-system role
indicators.notes: Uppercase headings and labels are valid when the reference or design system defines them. Reproduce them faithfully, including tracking and size.

indicators.name: Unrequested gradient backgrounds
indicators.summary: Mesh, aurora, radial glow and decorative linear gradients added to make a flat page feel premium.
signals: mesh or aurora gradient background
radial glow behind the hero
linear-gradient on page sections with no reference
animated gradient blobs
indicators.notes: A gradient can be functional, such as a text-protection scrim over photography. That requires a reference or requirement, not a colour pair chosen for atmosphere.

indicators.name: Unnecessary periods in titles
indicators.summary: Full stops appended to headings and card titles to imitate an editorial voice.
signals: heading text ending in a full stop
terminal periods on card titles
periods added to match a stylistic rhythm
sentence punctuation on navigation labels
indicators.notes: The reference may punctuate headings deliberately. A single full stop on a display heading is a decision to copy, not to invent.
